overview.about: The Mexico City Grand Prix is run at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, the highest-altitude circuit in Formula 1 at around 2,240 metres above sea level. The thin air cuts downforce and challenges engine cooling, while the stadium section - where the track snakes through a baseball arena packed with fans - creates one of the sport's best atmospheres. First held in 1963 and revived in 2015, it is a modern favourite. The 2026 race is on 30 October - 1 November.
overview.nextEvent: The 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix runs 30 October - 1 November. The altitude means engines, brakes and cooling work unusually hard, and the very long main straight into a tight first corner produces frequent first-lap drama in front of a huge home crowd.

@graph.description: The Mexico City Grand Prix is held at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, named for racing brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez. The circuit has hosted Formula 1 across several eras, beginning with a World Championship race in 1963, and its high altitude shapes car cooling, power-unit performance and race strategy. The stadium section gives the event a recognisable atmosphere as cars pass through the former baseball stadium. The existing OneSliders event page supplies the edition date through Event JSON-LD, which is retained here as the source-backed calendar. Practice, qualifying and the Grand Prix form the sporting programme; official organisers publish the detailed timetable and entry information for each edition.
